title: Rethinking Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Visual Domain Adaptation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The six per-task accuracies reported for OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC in Table 1 (96.1, 95.3, 77.6, 98.1, 77.1, 99.1) sum to 543.3, giving a mean of 90.55, yet the table reports the average as 90.1. Every other row of Table 1 is internally consistent to within 0.05 of rounding. Worse, the identical method on the identical dataset/features (OGLP+JMMD-HSIC, Office-31, ResNet-50) is reported as 91.5 in both the ablation Table 3 and the label-kernel Table 4. The same quantity thus appears as 90.1 (Table 1 average), 90.6 (computed from Table 1 cells), and 91.5 (Tables 3/4) - a 1.4-point spread that is material to the paper's central performance claims.

The text states: 'our proposed approach is better than the baseline methods SPL and OGL2P on average, and has achieved 1.4%/0.8% and 0.9%/0.8% improvements on the two datasets, respectively.' The 0.8% improvement over OGL2P on Office-31 is contradicted by the paper's own Table 1: OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC is 90.1 (or 90.6 computed from its cells), which is BELOW the OGL2P baseline's 90.7 - a 0.6% decrease, not a 0.8% improvement. The claimed OGL2P improvement holds only for Office-Home (73.6 vs 72.8 = +0.8%).

The text claims 'OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC achieves the best average results among all compared approaches, with 0.3% and 0.5% improvements over the second-best method, i.e., RSDA-MSTN.' On Office-31 (Table 1), the best average is RSDA-MSTN (91.2); OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC (90.1) ranks below both SPL+JMMD-HSIC (91.0) and RSDA-MSTN (91.2), so the claimed 0.3% improvement over RSDA-MSTN is unsupported. The 0.5% improvement holds only for Office-Home (OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC 73.6 vs RSDA-MSTN 73.1).

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 6 (Office10-Caltech10), OGL2P+Our row; Appendix F text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The 12 cells of the OGL2P+Our row in Table 6 sum to 1134.5, giving a mean of 94.54 (≈94.5), but the table reports 94.3 ± 0.7 - a discrepancy of 0.24 beyond rounding (all other rows are within 0.05). Appendix F additionally claims OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC 'achieves the best average results among all compared approaches, obtaining 0.4% and 0.7% improvements compared with the second-best method, i.e., OGL2P', yet the same table lists OGL2P at 94.6, above OGL2P+Our's reported 94.3 (a -0.3% difference, not +0.4%).

summary: Exhaustive verification (lenient strictness) of the paper 'Rethinking Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Visual Domain Adaptation'. The mathematical derivations (concise JMMD/HSIC in RKHS and projected RKHS, Theorem 1 uniformity K^1/K^2/K^3 special cases, graph-embedding sign analysis, and the reproducing-kernel PSD proofs in the appendix) were checked and found internally consistent. The core problems are statistical/data-integrity issues in the experimental results section: (1) Table 1's OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC average (90.1) does not match its own cells (90.55) and contradicts the same method/dataset reported as 91.5 in Tables 3 and 4; (2) Section 4.2's claim that the approach beats the OGL2P baseline on Office-31 with a 0.8% improvement is contradicted by Table 1, which shows OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC (90.1) below OGL2P (90.7); (3) Section 4.2's claim that OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC achieves the best average results with a 0.3% improvement over RSDA-MSTN is unsupported on Office-31, where RSDA-MSTN (91.2) is the best; and (4) Table 6's OGL2P+Our average (94.3) does not match its cells (94.5) and its claimed 0.4% improvement over OGL2P is contradicted by the same table (OGL2P = 94.6). A minor note: reference [55] lists publication year 2022 while the actual TNNLS issue is 2023, and carries an unusual editorial note; both are bibliographic-format issues not treated as critical. Because three findings carry confidence >= 0.85, the verdict is NEEDS_CORRECTION.
